dod_intent_evidence: Two 2023 Air Force SBIR Phase IIs plus an $18M 2025 USAF Phase II for the Mega Class satellite — SBIR record and news sections.
score_evidence: 'The Mega Class platform delivers 10x the power of other constellation class satellites (20kW vs. 2kW), unlocking industry-leading payload performance' — spec-brag framing, kW as the headline → lab_language_intensity (homepage)
'ultra-high-power spacecraft capable of delivering over 115kW of power and 15,000kg of payload mass to enable previously unattainable capabilities' → lab_language_intensity (sbir_abstract)

'We believe in ownership: if you design it, you see it fly. Pride comes from real hardware, not slide decks' — the story ends at launch; no mission operators, no Space Force users, no ground crews anywhere in ~1,541 words → operator_absence (homepage/about)

Open roles are entirely build-and-test hardware engineering (thermal, avionics test, optomechanical); zero mission-ops, ISSO, compliance, or government-integration roles → hiring_profile_skew (job_post list)
'K2 Space raises $110 million to scale up satellite production' — cash-rich with an SES anchor partnership; little visible clock pressure → stage_pressure kept low (news)

blind_spots.blind_spot: The ISR pitch never touches the government ground segment: tasking, C2, and data dissemination into existing Space Force/IC architectures
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 115kW ISR bus is judged by whether its payload data reaches an analyst through accredited ground infrastructure; integrating into SSC/NRO ground systems, getting an ATO for the C2 software they write in-house, and interoperating with legacy mission-management stacks is a multi-year gauntlet their language never acknowledges
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founding team is SpaceX-avionics and startup-exit DNA — vertical hardware integration is the religion ('80% of each satellite is built in-house'); ground-segment accreditation is someone else's plumbing until a Phase II demo stalls on it
blind_spots.evidence_quote: ultra-high-power spacecraft capable of delivering over 115kW of power and 15,000kg of payload mass to enable previously unattainable capabilities spanning ISR

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Build Bigger' runs head-on into the proliferated-resilience doctrine their USAF customer actually buys against — and their language never argues survivability beyond radiation
blind_spots.operator_reality: SDA/USSF moved to proliferated small constellations precisely because a single large satellite is a single large target; a Mega/Giga bus carrying a concentrated DoD payload must answer maneuver, ASAT threat, and graceful-degradation questions in acquisition review, not just radiation tolerance
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their resilience vocabulary is environmental ('withstand even the harshest radiation environments'), inherited from commercial GEO thinking; contested-space survivability is a warfighting frame their commercial SES-anchored messaging has no reason to use — until the Phase II customer does
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Bigger satellites deliver more power to payloads, mass on orbit, and resilience at lower cost. Bigger isn't excess, it's access.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No export-control or security language anywhere, from a company shipping satellite buses with DoD ISR ambitions
blind_spots.operator_reality: ITAR flow-down, CUI handling on the factory floor, and CMMC apply the moment USAF payload interface data hits their 289-person vertically integrated factory; a single spill or a failed CMMC assessment stalls the $18M Phase II and the SES-adjacent government pipeline behind it
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: In ~1,541 words of own language there is zero mention of ITAR, CMMC, or classified/CUI handling — the site is written for commercial operators and recruits, and compliance has never yet been the gate they died on
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 80% of each satellite is built in-house. Vertical integration drives reliability, accelerates production, and enables continuous innovation

opener_hook: K2's $18M USAF Mega Class Phase II will be judged on accredited ground-segment integration and contested-space survivability — two topics that appear nowhere in K2's own 1,500 words of public language.
what_they_do: Builds very large, high-power satellite buses (Mega/Giga Class) in a vertically integrated factory for commercial and USAF customers.
